advances: An obstruction for a target measure built with prescribed uniform endpoint probabilities and the entire smaller mass. It gives no upper bound for original mixed depth, and does not constrain nonuniform endpoint allocations or multiple targets.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The lifted hull projects onto $[-1,1]$ and the extreme sections are the prescribed endpoints. Its middle section is the convex hull of $T$ and the endpoint midpoint body $A\subset T$, hence is exactly $T$. The positive-area middle and an endpoint off its plane give full dimension. Let $c=|T|=1/2$, $a=|(2-s)A|$, $b=|sA|$, $e=32s^2/125=604028929/4294967296000$, and $\delta=(128/125)2^{-20}$. Direct area scaling gives $b=ce$, $a=c(1+e-\delta)$ and $M=c(2+2e-\delta)$. Since $0<\delta<2e$ and $e<1/6250$, the three masses are below $M/2$, $a>b$, and each extreme base has more than half the mass on its opposite side. Thus zero is the unique weighted median base.

Write $X=(2-s)U$ and $Y=sV$ with both $U,V$ uniform on $A$, and $Z=(X+Y)/2=\alpha U+(1-\alpha)V$, where $\alpha=1-s/2$. No independence is assumed. Set $a_0=1/3-e/16$, $b_0=1/3-41e/125$, $u=5a_0/4$ and $v=5(a_0+b_0)/4$. From $9/64000<e<1/6250$ and $3/128<s<1/40$ follow $1-\alpha<u<1$, $2/5<v/\alpha<1$, $8/25<b_0<1$ and $0<a_0<a_0+b_0<1$.

For $0\le r\le1$, the uniform marginal tail $\mathbb P(U_x/(4/5)\ge r)$ is $(1-r)^2$ by the similar corner triangle. For $2/5\le r\le1$, the tail $\mathbb P((U_x+U_y)/(4/5)>r)$ is $(1-r)^2/(3/5)$, because the normalized vertex heights are $0,2/5,1$ and the top corner retains fractions $1-r$ and $(1-r)/(3/5)$ of its two edges. The uniform probability of any cutting line is zero. If $Z_x\ge a_0$ then $U_x/(4/5)\ge (u-(1-\alpha))/\alpha$, since $V_x\le4/5$. Also $Z_y\le8/25$. If $(U_x+U_y)/(4/5)>v/\alpha$ then $Z_x+Z_y>a_0+b_0$ since $V_x+V_y\ge0$. This last strict implication bounds the mass of the complementary closed cap even for singular midpoint laws.

The three closed halfplanes $x\ge a_0$, $y\ge b_0$, $x+y\le a_0+b_0$ cover $\mathbb R^2$. The preceding bounds and the exact similar-triangle cap areas in $T$ give their respective masses divided by $c$ at most
$$
U_1=(1-a_0)^2+e((1-u)/\alpha)^2,\quad U_2=(1-b_0)^2,\quad
U_3=(a_0+b_0)^2+e\left[1-\frac{((\alpha-v)/\alpha)^2}{3/5}\right].
$$
Set $\tau=2M/(9c)$. Substitution gives the following numerators and denominators for the three gaps; for each pair $(N,D)$ the integer comparison $10^7N>6D$ holds.

| Gap | $N$ | $D$ |
|---|---:|---:|
| $\tau-U_1$ | 1432514278136662974050522862997520267 | 912835900916101579792855125196800000000000 |
| $\tau-U_2$ | 2025814712493388791956711 | 2594073385365405696000000000000 |
| $\tau-U_3$ | 5478570717192890979361486970803017356213 | 8557836571088452310558016798720000000000000000 |

Every possible center lies in at least one of the three caps. The same strictly subtarget upper bound $c\max_i U_i<2M/9-3/10^7$ applies for all centers and all couplings.

statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}\lbrace(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\rbrace$, $A=\operatorname{conv}\lbrace(0,0),(4/5,0),(0,8/25)\rbrace$ and $s=3/128+2^{-20}$. Lift $(2-s)A,T,sA$ to the bases $-1,0,1$ and take their convex hull. These are its exact integer fibers, each of positive area less than half the total mixed area $M$, and zero is the unique weighted median base. For every coupling of the uniform probabilities $X$ on $(2-s)A$ and $Y$ on $sA$, the planar measure $\eta=\mathbf1_T\,dx+|sA|\operatorname{Law}((X+Y)/2)$ satisfies
$$
\sup_{w\in\mathbb R^2}\inf_{H\ni w}\eta(H)<\frac{2M}{9}-\frac3{10^7},
$$
where $H$ ranges over closed planar halfspaces.
title: Every uniform endpoint coupling can miss the target depth
